Consult Summary:
32-year-old male doctor presents with 6–8 weeks of recurrent, transient right-sided numbness/weakness and gait change; concern for transient ischaemic attacks. Urgent referral to TIA clinic arranged; advised ED attendance if symptoms persist or worsen.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Recurrent unilateral neurological episodes – ?Transient Ischaemic Attack (TIA)
- Timeline: Began ~1½–2 months ago; initially weekly to monthly, now several times per day.
- Episode features (each lasting “a few days” then resolving):
  • Pins and needles/numbness in right hand.  
  • Subjective weakness in right arm and right leg; colleague noted altered gait.  
  • Recent difficulty holding cup and mild throat sensation during episodes; no dysarthria, persistent dysphagia, or visual disturbance.  
  • Associated fatigue, generalised weakness, intermittent nausea.  
- Pertinent negatives: No persistent dysphagia, speech difficulty, or vision change; no current symptoms at consult.
- Family history: Father underwent carotid endarterectomy for stroke prevention.
- Examination: None performed (video lost). No vitals documented.
- Impression: Suspected TIAs; urgent stroke assessment required.

Issue 2: Aspirin use without medical recommendation
- Current medication: Aspirin 75 mg orally once daily (self-initiated after father’s surgery).  
- No prior GP counselling on risks/benefits; needs review after specialist assessment.

Issue 3: Cerebrovascular risk assessment / prevention
- Family history as above; patient otherwise healthy, non-smoker, normotensive, normal prior cholesterol and diabetes screen (per patient report).  
- Requires formal risk evaluation and lifestyle/medical optimisation post-TIA work-up.

Medications:
- Aspirin 75 mg once daily.

Allergies:
- Penicillin (reaction details not documented).

Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Plastic surgery doctor.  
- Lives with wife.  
- Non-smoker; alcohol intake not discussed.

Preventative History:
- No information on vaccinations or screening tests documented.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed / not documented (video connection lost).  
- No vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Urgent referral sent to local TIA clinic; expected appointment within 1–2 days (by Thu/Fri).  
- Investigations anticipated: Carotid duplex ultrasound, brain imaging, additional stroke work-up.  
- Provide patient with TIA clinic and PALS contact numbers; advised to phone to confirm scheduling.  
- Safety-net advice: Attend ED immediately if symptoms recur and are prolonged or stronger; contact GP service for interim episodes/questions.  
- Medication review: Continue aspirin until specialist review (implicit; not explicitly discussed).  
- Document referral and contact details in notes.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing expected elements: vitals, physical/neuro examination, alcohol history, full allergy details (reaction type), formal medication reconciliation beyond aspirin.  
● No internal conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: Mostly clear; occasional audio/video loss prevented examination.
